title: A holomorphic symmetric pair admits the explicit infinite-order differential intertwiner determined by an equivariant normal-space polynomial, with compact-uniform convergence and holomorphic extension for a subgroup holomorphic discrete series
author: Ryosuke Nakahama
source_title: Construction of Intertwining Operators  between Holomorphic Discrete Series Representations
difficulty_reason: The proof must turn abstract branching data into an actual operator whose infinitely many differential terms converge on holomorphic functions. The author derives a new equivariant Bergman kernel, identifies its differential symbol using the symmetric-pair quasi-inverse formula, and supplies Cauchy and dilation estimates controlling the entire derivative series. Holomorphic extension beyond the initial norm-sum convergence region is also justified, so the result goes beyond a formal intertwining identity.

proof_review.note: The full embedding construction in Theorem3.10(2) and its convergence/extension theorem3.12(2) were read with Sections3.1–3.3. The author constructs the Bergman/quasi-inverse kernel from the prescribed equivariant normal-space polynomial, proves its transformation law and uniqueness, converts its integral realization to an explicit infinite-order differential operator, and uses Cauchy bounds and central dilation to prove compact-uniform convergence before extending holomorphically to the entire ambient domain. The prior branching/discrete-decomposability results and Jordan triple identities are background; the new kernel and convergence arguments are supplied here. Select this embedding construction once, not separate projection or individual symmetric-pair formula variants.

statement_scope: The embedding branch of Theorem3.10(2), with the convergence and extension conclusion of Theorem3.12(2). G is connected real reductive with each simple noncompact component Hermitian; G_1 is the connected Cartan-stable symmetric subgroup of holomorphic type, containing the complex-structure element z. Use the stated universal covers, finite-dimensional irreducible compact-complex modules (tau,V),(rho,W), positive-definite representation inner products and holomorphic highest-weight realizations; require H_rho(D_1,W) to be a holomorphic discrete series. rho occurs in P(p_2^+) tensor V restricted to K_1^C, and K(x_2) is the specified polynomial satisfying (3.3). The kernel symbol in Theorem3.10(2) defines the (g_1,K_1)-intertwiner on finite vectors; for all subgroup holomorphic functions its derivative series converges compact-uniformly on |x_1|_infty+|x_2|_infty<1 and extends holomorphically and continuously to the whole D. No singular-parameter meromorphic continuation or separate projection branch is selected.
editorial_warning: Theorem3.10(2) has alternative hypotheses; this packet explicitly selects the holomorphic-discrete subgroup alternative needed for the all-holomorphic-functions convergence claim. In the integration display leading to (3.6), B(x_1) appears inside the y_1 integral, while the preceding norm definition and subsequent finite constant use B(y_1); this bounded variable typo is preserved in the original pages and distinguished from the author theorem.
